answer: The sky is blue mainly because of the way the Earth blocks most sunlight at ground level. When the sun is low, it cannot penetrate through the lower atmosphere, so the only light reaching our eyes is the violet and blue portions that have been scattered more. Once those rays reach the surface, they mix to appear mostly white throughout the day, and much of the blue light is absorbed by the ground or blocked by clouds.
